description: Canonical signature algorithm vocabulary for v1 proof alg and raw signature_algorithm fields.
registry_rules: Schema enum values for proof alg fields MUST be generated from active rows' proof_alg only when publishing a new schema version, then frozen for that schema version.

Schema enum values for raw signature_algorithm fields MUST be generated from active rows' signature_algorithm only when publishing a new schema version, then frozen for that schema version. Activating a reserved/new algorithm requires a new schema version and profile negotiation; registry activation MUST NOT expand an existing schema enum in place (zh/conformance/schema-registry.md §6.1 b.1).
Algorithms not present as active rows MUST fail closed with unsupported_signature_alg on critical proofs.

A reserved hybrid row is a single negotiated verification policy over two independent proof entries, not a new unregistered compact signature encoding. Both components MUST bind the same canonical payload and proof purpose; accepting a stripped single component as hybrid-verified is forbidden.

algorithms.security_note: Classical Ed25519 default signature suite; not post-quantum.
Classical ECDSA P-256 suite for WebAuthn/FIDO2 and PKI interop.

NIST FIPS 204 ML-DSA category 3 suite for post-quantum hardening profiles. JOSE/JWK serialization follows RFC 9964: alg=ML-DSA-65, kty=AKP, required pub, optional private seed in priv, and empty ML-DSA context.

activation_requirements: Publish canonical proof-set ordering and duplicate-component rejection rules
Publish anti-stripping vectors proving that both components bind identical canonical payload bytes and proof purpose and that either missing/invalid component fails hybrid verification
Define verifier capability tiers and downgrade display semantics without ever reporting a single-component result as hybrid verified
Publish a new negotiated proof contract release; reserved policy MUST NOT widen frozen proof_alg or signature_algorithm enums in place
algorithms.security_note: Reserved hybrid verification policy. Before activation, the canonical_id itself is not a wire alg and MUST fail closed if presented as one; active Ed25519 and ML-DSA-65 proofs retain their independent existing semantics.
